steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been going since you finished your cellulite reduction treatments with us? Is the skin still looking smooth and toned in the areas we treated and you're loving how it looks, has a little started to creep back, or are you pretty much back to where you were before you started with us?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Doing Great: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
I love hearing that, {{contact_first_name}}. That’s exactly what we want. There’s nothing better than putting on the shorts or the swimsuit and not giving it a second thought.

Do you remember how much it bothered you before we worked on it? The outfits you avoided, the angles you didn’t want in photos? (Let them answer. Let them relive the win before you move on.)

steps.title: Starting to Creep Back
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's completely normal. The dimpling and texture naturally work their way back once treatments stop; it's not anything you did wrong, and it is exactly why we check in. I remember how great you looked and felt and how proud you were. What do you think made it come back? Was it cost, life getting busy, or something else?

Let them answer, be warm and non-judgmental, and do NOT try to book yet.

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Before
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's completely normal. The dimpling and texture naturally work their way back once treatments stop; it's not anything you did wrong, and it is exactly why we check in. I remember how great you looked and felt and how proud you were. What do you think made it come back? Was it cost, life getting busy, or something else?

Let them answer, be warm and non-judgmental, and do NOT try to book yet.

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes. Almost everyone says yes. You asked permission, and it’s their file. And remember why these questions matter: most clients come in for one area and never think to mention anything else. They have no idea how much we can actually do. The questions are how you find that out.)

steps.title: The Transition: Acknowledge and Ask Permission
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, obviously I know you said the area we treated is starting to bother you again, and we’re absolutely going to talk about that. But while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so your file is completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Critical: write down every area they mention as you go. You’ll recap them in a moment.)

First, and be honest with yourself here. When you’re getting dressed or catching yourself in the mirror, is there any OTHER area that’s started catching your eye? For most of our clients it’s the backs of the thighs, the buttocks, or that spot just above the knees. The one you only see in certain lighting.

How about how things look in your favorite leggings or shorts? Anything that’s changed about how they fit or how you feel wearing them?

Any changes in skin texture or firmness anywhere? That dimpled, “orange peel” look showing up somewhere new, or skin that just doesn’t feel as smooth and tight as it used to?

And is there anything coming up on the calendar. A beach trip, a wedding, a reunion, a season you want to feel completely confident for?

(If they mentioned anything at all, recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

Now {{contact_first_name}}, you just told me about those areas. If you could completely smooth just one of them and never think about it again, which one would you choose?

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, what I’d like to do now is ask you a few quick questions about {{main_concern}}, so I can get your file fully updated. It’ll only take a minute.

(Take the concern they named and make it real with three questions, in order. Pause after each and let them fully answer.)

How long has that been on your mind? A few weeks, a couple months, longer?

(Let them answer, then:) “[Repeat their answer back]? That’s a long time to have something quietly chipping away at how you feel about yourself. Would you agree that’s not really OK?”

Is it something you notice here and there, or pretty much every time you look in the mirror at this point? (Let them answer. “That’s a lot.”)

And the last thing I’d like to ask is how it affects you day to day. But first, do me a favor: think of a day you felt really good about how you looked, maybe an event, an outfit that worked, photos you actually liked. Now think of a day it really got to you. Do you have those two days in your head?

(Wait for the yes. Then:) “On that harder day, how does it change things? What you wear, how comfortable you feel around people, at work, out with friends?” (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that with me. It makes complete sense, and that’s exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long, how often, how it affects them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like you'd really just love to get back to looking and feeling the way you did when you finished your treatments. Is that fair to say?

(About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment.)

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds to me like {{main_concern}} isn’t just a small thing. It may also be affecting how comfortable and confident you feel around the people in your life. Do you see how that could be the case?

(Wait for their answer. If they say no or hesitate: “That’s completely fair, but it’s clearly been on your mind, and that’s reason enough.” Then continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you set up with an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look and see if there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to help you with {{main_concern}}. If {{rec_pronoun}} can help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think it’s the right fit, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know that as well, because {{rec_pronoun}}’re not here to waste anybody’s time or money. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you did mention {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is the timing just not right, or is there something else on your mind that's holding you back from taking a look?

(Warm and easygoing, no pressure, and never restate the concern back at them. You're just trying to understand what's in the way. Then stop and let them answer.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: Nothing Found: The Commitment Question
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I am so glad everything is still looking so good, and we’re thrilled to hear it.

Let me ask you this. I remember when you first came in, you told us it wasn’t about anyone else. It was about feeling completely confident in your own skin, in anything you wanted to wear. Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Don’t argue with whatever they say. Acknowledge it warmly.)

And {{contact_first_name}}, here’s the thing about the results. They’re so much easier to maintain than to rebuild. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Now that we’ve updated your file, let’s get you in for a quick check-in session so you keep the results you worked for. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: It came back after I stopped
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that can happen from time to time, because the texture tends to return gradually once you're off your treatments. That's exactly why coming in makes sense, so {{rec_pronoun}} can look at the whole picture and talk through the best plan to get you back on track and help you hold your results.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I’m embarrassed it came back
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don't be. There's truly no judgment here. The dimpling naturally works its way back once treatments stop. That's just how skin behaves, it's not anything you did wrong. It's exactly why we reach out. {{rec_pronoun_cap}}'d simply love to help you get back to where you were.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Did it even work last time?
steps.content:
That's a completely fair question, and it's exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}}'ll want to talk through in person, so {{rec_pronoun}} can look at the whole picture and what would help it hold. (Never make guaranteed-results claims on the call.)

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

The nice thing is, coming in is really just information. You'd get a look at what's possible and exactly what it would involve, and then you get to decide with real answers instead of wondering. No pressure either way.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't really show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for: you get a look at your options and answers that actually apply to you. So let me get you on the schedule first, no pressure, and you'll have real answers to go on.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?
